growth_story.headline: Morocco's income per person has climbed at about 2.3 percent a year since 1990, through droughts, a 2020 slump and a new burst of public building.
growth_story.arc: Morocco's income per person has risen since 1990 with no lasting change of pace: growth averaged 2.3 percent a year over 1990–2025, and income per person reached its highest level yet, about 3,644 dollars in constant terms, in 2025. In the 1990s growth swung widely from year to year, from 8.9 percent in 1994 to minus 6.9 in 1995 and 10.6 in 1996. The World Bank credits market-oriented reforms from the late 1990s and a stable policy framework with steadier growth after 2000, and income per person grew 3.0 percent a year over 2006–2015. Growth then eased to 1.6 percent a year over 2016–2025, which the World Bank links to fading reform momentum; it also finds that growth has leaned more and more on capital rather than on higher productivity. That decade includes a fall of 8.1 percent in 2020, when the pandemic struck alongside a severe drought, and a climb to 3.6 percent in 2025 on a harvest recovery and large public works.

growth_story.tension: The World Bank describes separate phases: a take-off in the 2000s, a slowdown in the 2010s and a pickup from 2023. In the data, income per person did grow faster over 2006–2015 (3.0 percent a year) than over 2016–2025 (1.6). But the tool's break test finds no lasting shift since 1990, only one era averaging 2.3 percent, because growth jumps so much from year to year. The World Bank also calls 2025 the strongest year in a decade. For income per person, the 3.6 percent of 2025 is below the 7.1 percent rebound of 2021.
